case_studies.title: PolicyGuard: From Organizational Policies to Neuro-SymbolicCompliance Review Engines
case_studies.abstract: Policy-grounded document review requires determining whether a target document complies with organization-specific policies, guidelines, or playbooks. While large language models can assist with policy interpretation and document analysis, end-to-end prompting leaves the applied policy logic implicit, making compliance decisions difficult to inspect, update, and test. We present PolicyGuard, a neuro-symbolic framework for policy-grounded document compliance review. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of ensuring documents comply with organisational policies by building a tool called PolicyGuard, which converts policy guidance into an executable review engine. The result is a more transparent and inspectable compliance review process. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: GR2 Technical Report
case_studies.abstract: Industrial recommendation systems serve billions of users through a multi-stage funnel -- retrieval, early-stage ranking, and re-ranking -- where the final re-ranking step disproportionately shapes user engagement and downstream performance, particularly for carousel and grid display formats. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of improving user engagement in industrial recommendation systems by focusing on the re-ranking stage, the authors built a system using Large Language Models, and the result is a potentially more effective way to shape user experience. The study aims to address gaps in industrial adoption of LLMs in recommendation systems. It explores the application of LLMs in the re-ranking stage, which is crucial for user engagement.

case_studies.title: RAISE: LLM-based Automated Heuristic Design with Robust Adversary Instance Search
case_studies.abstract: Automated Heuristic Design (AHD) with Large Language Models (LLMs) has shown remarkable progress in discovering high-quality heuristics. However, existing LLM-based AHD methods optimize heuristics for a fixed training instance set and may fail catastrophically when deployed under real-world distributional shifts. We propose Robust Adversary Instance Search (RAISE), a framework that integrates constrained worst-case instance search within a principled neighborhood of the training distribution into the LLM-based evolutionary search loop. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of large language models failing when faced with real-world changes by creating a framework called RAISE, which helps find robust heuristics. The result is a more reliable way to design heuristics using large language models. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: JETO-Bench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Execution Time Improvement Patches in Java
case_studies.abstract: Automated fixing of performance issues is gaining increasing attention. However, existing benchmarks of execution time improvement patches are fixed datasets that target Python, C++, or .NET and cannot be extended to new patches according to user-defined configurations. In this paper, we present JETO-Mine, the first configurable and reusable tool for automatically creating reproducible benchmarks of execution time improvement patches (ETIPs) in real-world Java projects. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of manually benchmarking execution time improvement patches in Java projects. The authors built JETO-Mine, a tool that automatically creates reproducible benchmarks for these patches. The result is a configurable and reusable tool that saves time and effort in evaluating performance improvements.

case_studies.title: When LLMs Read Tables Carelessly: Measuring and Reducing Data Referencing Errors
case_studies.abstract: While large language models (LLMs) perform well on table tasks, they still make data referencing errors (DREs), i.e., incorrectly citing or omitting table values, despite understanding the table structure. Beyond final-answer accuracy, DREs directly compromise the correctness and reliability of intermediate reasoning steps. Yet prior studies have only offered limited, small-scale analyses. In this work, we present the first systematic evaluation of tabular data referencing errors across different models and tasks. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of data referencing errors in large language models, where the models incorrectly cite or omit table values. The authors built a systematic evaluation of tabular data referencing errors across different models and tasks. The result shows that these errors occur across all tested models, compromising the correctness and reliability of intermediate reasoning steps.

case_studies.title: A Lifecycle and Application-Stack Survey of Large Language Model Vulnerabilities: Attacks, Risks, Defenses, and Open Problems
case_studies.abstract: Large language models are no longer only text generators. They are increasingly embedded in retrieval pipelines, enterprise assistants, coding environments, robotic systems, security-operation workflows, and autonomous agents that can read private data, call tools, write files, execute code, and act across organizational boundaries. This shift changes the security problem: risks do not arise from the model weights alone, but from the full lifecycle and application stack through which data, prompts, model outputs, tools, memories, and user authority interact. case_studies.summary: This research identifies security risks in large language models, which are increasingly used in various applications, and provides a comprehensive overview of vulnerabilities, attacks, and defenses. The authors built a framework to analyze the lifecycle and application stack of large language models, revealing potential risks that arise from the interaction of data, prompts, and user authority. The result is a better understanding of the security problems associated with large language models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that uses large language models, here is what to do: review your application stack for potential security risks, check for vulnerabilities in your data pipelines, and assess the interactions between user authority and model outputs to mitigate potential attacks.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper addresses a critical issue with the increasing deployment of large language models, which affects IT engineers working with these models. It scores 16 for real-world impact as it reveals actionable insights about vulnerabilities and open problems. Overall, it's a relevant and impactful paper.

case_studies.title: FinPersona-Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal Psychometric Stability of Autonomous Financial Agents
case_studies.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous financial agents initialized with explicit behavioral mandates such as "preserve capital" or "avoid speculative bets" that are meant to govern every decision throughout deployment. In practice, however, as market context accumulates over long horizons, these mandates gradually lose their behavioral influence, a phenomenon we formalize as Mandate Salience Decay (MSD). case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of autonomous financial agents straying from their initial behavioral mandates over time, creating a benchmark called FinPersona-Bench to measure this decay. The result is a tool to evaluate the stability of financial agents in simulated markets. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: FARS: A Fully Automated Research System Deployed at Scale
case_studies.abstract: Recent automated research systems show that language-model agents can generate hypotheses, run experiments, and write complete manuscripts, but most evidence still comes from selected examples, human-framed topics, or a few pre-defined research tasks. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of automating the research process by building a fully automated AI-for-AI research system called FARS, which can generate and advance projects across research topics at scale, resulting in a system that can work autonomously. The system uses stage-specific agents to coordinate tasks and record proposals. This research is not directly applicable to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs
case_studies.abstract: Metacognition is a critical component of intelligence that describes the ability to monitor and regulate one's own cognitive processes. Yet LLMs exhibit systemic deficiencies in key metacognitive faculties: they hallucinate with high confidence, fail to recognize knowledge boundaries, and misrepresent their internal uncertainty--undermining trustworthiness and reliability. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of large language models (LLMs) providing overconfident and inaccurate results by building a system that uses reinforcement learning with metacognitive feedback, resulting in more accurate uncertainty expression. The researchers built a model that can monitor its own performance and adapt its behavior accordingly. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.
